title: He Wants AI Benchmarking To Be a Science, Not a Dark Art

problems: insight 1 has a figure, so its body must be <= 20 words; it has 27. Cut 7+ words or drop the figure

figure on slide 2: "Same model scores 90% on one dataset and 73% on another" is not supported by SOURCE. The 90% vs 73% is a hypothetical example, not real data; the figure presents it as a real measured result ('Same model'), so it should be labeled illustrative/hypothetical.

claims.claim: AI test scores (benchmark scores) are shaky
claims.evidence_quote: If you look at a model’s accuracy numbers on one benchmark, and then you change the test set only slightly, you get completely different accuracy numbers.

claims.claim: Rankings of models are not shaky (stable)
claims.evidence_quote: those rankings tend to be very stable across different datasets.

claims.claim: Changing a test set only slightly makes accuracy numbers come out completely different
claims.evidence_quote: you change the test set only slightly, you get completely different accuracy numbers.

claims.claim: Same model scores 90% on one dataset and 73% on another
claims.evidence_quote: If you have 90% accuracy on one dataset and 73% on another, which is it? I have no idea how good this model is.
claims.problem: The 90% vs 73% is a hypothetical example, not real data; the figure presents it as a real measured result ('Same model'), so it should be labeled illustrative/hypothetical.

claims.claim: Rankings hold up; order tends to stay stable across datasets when comparing models
claims.evidence_quote: those rankings tend to be very stable across different datasets.

claims.claim: The 90% model still beats the 80% model, even on different data
claims.evidence_quote: If one model gets 90% on a particular test set, and another model gets 80%, then the 90% model is the model you’d want to use in the real world. It’ll still do better on other datasets, even ones that are quite different than the test set.

claims.claim: Rankings only hold if models train on the same data
claims.evidence_quote: The stability of model rankings has one big caveat: Models need to train on the same training set.

claims.claim: We don't know what LLMs were trained on
claims.evidence_quote: But we don’t know what LLMs were trained on.

claims.claim: Builders can tailor data to boost benchmark results
claims.evidence_quote: model builders can strategically assemble data mixes that best promote benchmark performance.

claims.claim: Models may study for the test
claims.evidence_quote: It’s a little bit like studying to the test, which we all do in high school.

claims.claim: Trust who ranks higher, not the score
claims.evidence_quote: We should avoid comparisons or conclusions that implicitly require the absolute number to make sense.

claims.claim: Rankings stay reliable only when every model gets the same kind of preparation
claims.evidence_quote: If everyone optimizes, or “altitude trains,” the absolute numbers will be inflated, but you can restore the validity of the rankings.

claims.claim: AI benchmarks are tests that score and rank models
claims.evidence_quote: you use the test set only to compare and rank models — to have a leaderboard
